newsitem.title: INDIA: Venezuela sees oil output at 5-6 mln bpd in 2005/6.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sees oil output at 5-6 mln bpd in 2005/6.

text.p: Venezuela's Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta reiterated on Wednesday his country plans to produce five to six million barrels per day (bpd) of oil by the year 2005/06.
"Our plan is to produce five to six million barrels per day by 2005/06. This is the production potential," Arrieta told a news conference in the Indian capital.
He said Venezuela was currently producing 2.48 million bpd. But its production potential stood at 3.2 million bpd, he added.
Venezuela has an OPEC quota of 2.359 million bpd but independent observers say it produced 3.15 million in October.
"Some people say we are violating our quota in OPEC. This is not true," Arrieta said.
Arrieta is in India to attend the fifth annual International Energy Conference in Goa being held from December 6 to 8.
He said the last four energy conferences were used as brain-storming sessions but he hoped the Goa conference would bring out some concrete proposals.
Representatives from 37 countries are expected to attend the conference of oil producers and consumers.
"Environment, taxation, trading among regions, technology are the likely the major issues to be discussed," Arrieta said.
Another important issue to be taken up is the use of natural gas as an efficient source of energy.

Venezuelan officials said that rising energy demand in southeast and east Asian countries like China, Japan, South Korea and South American countries like Argentina and Brazil would change the face of the hydrocarbon market.
Arrieta said the question was how to deal with this change.
Arrieta met Indian officials in New Delhi and said Venezuela has offered to cooperate in power and petroleum sector.
"There are many opportunities and spaces where India and Venezuela could interact for benefit of both the nations," Arrieta said.
